summary: First full test pass of Dehla Pakad against the public URL. Backend: added tests/test_multiuser_api.py (18 tests, all passing). It covers 401 on protected endpoints, WS rejecting a bad token, the full private-room flow (create, non-member 404, friend invite, non-friend invite 403, join, non-host settings/start 403, seat swap, invalid seats 400, dealer/target, start blocked until everyone is ready, start, double start rejected), game-state privacy across all 4 seats, outsider GET game 404, active game blocking new room/queue (409), wrong player choosing trump rejected, trump selection, out-of-turn play rejected, playing a card you don't hold rejected, a legal play, WS chat + reaction + chat history, forfeit -> match_over + history, and public matchmaking with 4 users auto-starting. Engine tests: 83 pass. UI (Playwright, 4 browser contexts signed in with Clerk sign-in tickets): landing page, Clerk sign-in form, onboarding (duplicate username rejected), dashboard (username, stats, rejoin banner shown while a match is active and gone after it ends), game table (4 seats, team labels, dealer badge, scoreboard, trump badge, turn indicator, Live status, only legal cards clickable: 3/13 or 4/13 when following suit, 0 enabled when it's not your turn), trump selection (only the seat right of the dealer sees the 4 options, the others see the waiting banner, hand goes from 5 to 13 cards), a full trick shown live to all 4 players, chat drawer + unread badge + emoji bubble over the seat, offline badges when a socket closes, Koth modal (declare -> KOTH badge for everyone), round result modal + 7s auto-advance to the next round, victory screen -> match history, the whole private lobby flow in the UI (code join, seat swap synced to others, dealer, target 10, ready x4, start enabled only when all are ready, everyone redirected to the same /game), public matchmaking in the UI (queue status, match-found toast, public lobby with no host controls, ready -> auto-start into the game), friends (search, request toast, accept, accepted toast, online dot), invite friend (toast with Join, dashboard invitation, accept -> lobby), settings (username, avatar, theme light/dark persists after reload, header toggle), history/leaderboard/profile pages showing data, and a mobile check of dashboard + table at 390x844. Two real backend design bugs found in public matchmaking lobbies (details below). No 500s in backend logs.

critical.endpoint: POST /api/matchmaking/join, POST /api/rooms (leave_all_lobbies -> _leave on a public room)
critical.issue: Public lobbies get stuck. If one of the 4 matched players leaves the public lobby (Leave room, re-queuing, or creating a private room), the other 3 are left in a public room with an empty seat and host_id=None. Nobody from the queue fills the seat, and no one can start (start returns 403). /matchmaking/status keeps returning that room_code, so they keep landing back in it. Reproduced: 4 users joined, 1 created a private room -> public room seats [p3, None, p2, p4], status 'lobby'; the 3 left readied but it never started.

A matched public room only starts when all 4 are ready, and there is no ready timeout. One idle or AFK player (for example someone who closed the tab right after the match-found toast) keeps the other 3 waiting forever. Suggest a ready deadline (e.g. 30-60s) that kicks unready players and either sends the ready ones back to the front of the queue or fills the seats from the queue.

minor.issue: Duplicate pending invitations are not deduplicated: inviting the same friend to the same room twice inserts two rows.
server.py is 737 lines, over the 700-line guideline. Split it into routers (friends, rooms, matchmaking, admin, ws).

FLAKY test, not a product bug: check_privacy() compares the four players' cached states, which can be at different seq values over real network latency. It reported 'leak 10H to seat 0' because a card already in the public trick was still in the stale hand of the player who played it. Engine view() only exposes the caller's own hand, plus partner_hand during the gs_decision phase. Fix the test to compare states with the same seq. Failed 1 of 1 runs on the public URL; passes on localhost.

issues: The center trick card overlaps the partner (top) seat's name plate and card-count chip. The partner's 'N cards' label is hidden while the other two seats show it. Push the trick area down or shrink the top seat on small screens.
A forfeited match shows only 'WIN/LOSS 0-1' with no 'Forfeit' marker, so it reads like a normal 1-point match.
The score is always shown A-B no matter which team the viewer was on.
A trophy icon is shown even on DEFEAT; use a neutral or defeat icon.
'Random teams' uses sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5), which is a biased shuffle. Use Fisher-Yates.

action_items: Fix public lobby dead-ends: when a player leaves a public room before the start, either dissolve the room and send the remaining players back to the front of the queue, or fill the seat from mm_queue. Also clear the stale room_code that /matchmaking/status returns.
Add a ready timeout for public lobbies so one AFK player can't block the other 3 forever.
Deduplicate pending invitations (same from_id, to_id, room_code).
Mobile table: keep the trick area from overlapping the partner seat.
Small copy/visual fixes: '1 round', a forfeit label in history, a defeat icon on the victory screen.
Make e2e_match.py check_privacy compare states with the same seq so it isn't flaky over network latency.
critical_code_review_comments: game_service._finish_match pops the game from memory, and later GETs read it from Mongo. That's fine, but the round_over timers in self.timers are never cleaned up after the match finishes (small leak).
ensure_free() calls mm_queue.remove() without holding mm_lock. That's a race with mm_join's pop loop (low risk on a single event loop, but inconsistent).

Koth rule as written: once Koth is declared, whichever team captures the 4th ten wins 2 points, even when that's the team holding 1 ten against 3. The modal copy matches this and it's consistent across the code; just confirm it's the intended house rule (we saw a round where Team B won Koth +2 with tens 3-1 against it).

The 'hello' message is sent after notify_presence broadcasts game_state, so clients can get game_state before hello. Harmless, but clients shouldn't assume hello comes first (our first helper script did).
Leaderboard has no pagination and fills up with e2e test users created by the test scripts (e2e####_N).

The public-lobby leave dead-end is the main bug to retest.
rca of the issue: Public lobby dead-end: mm_join builds a room from 4 queued uids with host_id=None. _leave() sets the leaving seat to None and, because the room is public, keeps host_id None. Nothing ever re-fills a public room's seats: mm_join only creates new rooms from mm_queue. set_ready only auto-starts when _all_ready (all seats filled), and start_game needs a host (_host_only raises 403 for public rooms). Result: the remaining 3 players are stuck. Reproduce: 4 users POST /matchmaking/join, then user 1 POSTs /rooms (or /rooms/{code}/leave), then the other 3 POST ready -> status stays 'lobby' forever. Fix: in _leave for public rooms, delete the room and push the remaining uids back to the front of mm_queue (sending them a 'requeued' WS event), or backfill from mm_queue under mm_lock.
